rounds.sentence: Mom looked outside and said, "It's raining cats and dogs!"

choices.text: It is raining very hard.
Cats and dogs are falling from the sky.
It is a warm, sunny day.

rounds.sentence: Sam smiled and said the puzzle was a piece of cake.

choices.text: He ate a slice of cake.
It was very easy to do.
It was much too hard.

rounds.sentence: "Hold your horses!" said Dad when I ran ahead.

choices.text: Grab the horses by the rope.
Run as fast as you can.
Wait a moment and be patient.

rounds.sentence: Tom stayed home because he felt under the weather.

choices.text: He felt sick today.
He stood below the rain clouds.
He felt happy and full of energy.

rounds.sentence: Before the show, I had butterflies in my stomach.

choices.text: Real butterflies were inside my stomach.
I felt nervous and excited.
I was very, very hungry.

rounds.sentence: After the long hike, we all hit the hay.

choices.text: We punched a pile of hay.
We made a big snack.
We went to bed to sleep.

rounds.idiom: let the cat out of the bag
rounds.sentence: Oops! Maya let the cat out of the bag about the surprise.

choices.text: She told the secret.
She let a cat climb out of a bag.
She lost her school bag.

rounds.sentence: On rainy days, my brother is a couch potato.

choices.text: He is a potato sitting on the couch.
He is lazy and watches a lot of TV.
He cooks potatoes all day long.

page_title.en: Gabby's Funny Sayings — What Does It Really Mean? (Grade 3)

page_intro.en: Gabby the goose loves funny sayings! When we say "it's raining cats and dogs," no animals are really falling — it just means it is raining hard. Read the saying, then tap what it REALLY means, not what the words literally say. A Grade 3 vocabulary game about figurative language, aligned to Common Core L.3.5.a.
